meta.weight_definition: Each directed edge weight is the count of links from source article to target article; duplicate directed pairs are summed.
meta.preprocessing: Duplicate directed source-target rows are summed before analysis. The unweighted representation assigns weight 1 to every distinct directed arc; the weighted representation uses the aggregated source-data weight. Both use all philosopher nodes, including isolates. Louvain runs on the directed graph with NetworkX directed modularity; Infomap is directed and receives each arc's weight. For each Infomap run, all nodes are explicitly added before links so isolates receive singleton modules rather than being omitted.
meta.settings: Louvain uses NetworkX louvain_communities with weight='weight', default resolution and threshold, and seeds 0–19; the highest-modularity run is kept for each representation. Infomap 2.15.1 uses directed=True with default flow settings and seeds 1–20; the lowest-codelength run is kept. Weighted and unweighted runs use identical settings within each algorithm.
meta.comparison: NMI is calculated on all 1,444 philosophers for each same-algorithm pair. Changed-node counts compare each philosopher's set of co-members, not numeric community IDs; arbitrary IDs are not aligned or treated as identities. Community size distributions include singleton communities.
meta.interpretation: Each edge weight counts links from one source Wikipedia article to another target article in the source dataset. It is not a measure of philosophical agreement, relationship strength, or historical importance.
